reason: Claim confirmed in code, but the action is broader than needed. tools/trainlab.py gates() (l.693-701) builds g['parity'], and decisions() (l.832-855) never reads it, so the in_force flags ignore parity. Which verdicts this affects: (1) K3b DeepCenter: every dc{t} arm is a 'presafe' replay (l.517-523), and aggregate() (l.576-582) takes delta = replay(t) minus the kernel's own final graph. If the presafe replay does not reproduce the kernel graph, that replay error is added to every dc delta, and so to t*, the plateau and L2. For K3b this is a real hole. (2) K3 forkmid is NOT affected: the forkmid45 arm is forkmid(control), and control is dump['final'], the kernel graph itself, with no replay. Gating K3 on parity would only block a valid verdict. (3) divins_graph_mismatch only affects the ins35* arms, which are warning-only under L5. There is a second, unflagged gap of the same kind: DCLookup (l.256-269) treats an unseen point as a missing score, which means accepted. Per-arm dc_miss is stored in info['dc{t}'] (l.523), but only the control-threshold presafe dc_miss is summed, and no decision uses it. So misses at t* or its neighbours silently inflate the forks added by the arc. Status: the exp60 dumps are downloaded and the main score has been running since about 20:19 UTC (_dl/trainlab_score.log). There is no results.json yet, so parity on real data is unknown. It has only been tested on a synthetic graph (tests/test_trainlab.py::test_end_to_end_replay_parity). This is an offline CPU tool. The fix does not touch any kernel, so byte-identity and fail-soft rules are not affected, R1-R10 still hold, and there is no runtime cost. It is an honesty fix, not a new mechanism.
fix: Before reading K3b, patch decisions() in tools/trainlab.py (additive; about 10 lines). Set par_ps = no 6bba clip with parity.presafe.writer_equal False. Set dcm = sum of r['arms'][f'dc{t:.2f}']['dc_miss'] over t* and its grid neighbours on 6bba clips. Then deepcenter_K3b.in_force = dc_now AND par_ps AND dcm == 0, and add fields 'parity_presafe_ok' and 'dc_miss_arc'. Leave forkmid_K3.in_force unchanged, because it runs on the kernel graph; only show parity next to it. Add divins_graph_mismatch to the insertion (L5) warnings. After the running score finishes: if parity.pass is True, all dc arcs have dc_miss == 0 and there are no divins mismatches, report 'parity clean' and nothing changes. Otherwise rerun `python tools/trainlab.py score --dumps _dl/exp60_a _dl/exp60_b --nb <lab nb> --only <parity-clean stems> --out experiments/exp60_trainlab/results_parityclean`. It needs its own --out: the default --out would overwrite results, and L2 cannot be recomputed from results.json because the fork lists are popped. Report both runs. K3b goes ahead only if it passes on the full set and on the parity-clean set, with the (now smaller) n_evaluable >= 6 still met. Also check that a clean replay at t = 0.25 reproduces the control. A cleaner variant of the arc takes the delta against that presafe replay rather than against the kernel graph; label it info-only so the pre-registered gate is not changed.
realistic_gain: 0 direct LB/private gain; this is insurance. It stops K3b (the DeepCenter threshold rider) from being built or submitted on a lab arc biased by replay mismatch or DC lookup misses. The chance that it fires is probably low: parity passed the synthetic end-to-end test, and the forkblob run on the same dumps completed. But it costs about 15 min of CPU and needs no kernel change. It has no effect on K3 forkmid, K2 or the insertion verdicts.
